title: autotune: default batching/caching + quantization profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ravi Patel
description: Summary: Adds an 'autotune' defaults engine that recommends batching and KV-caching defaults, ships a curated set of quantization profiles for common model families, and ramps up a small unit-economics (uecon) toolkit exposed as an internal CLI and API endpoint. Motivation: customers frequently ask for safe defaults to reduce token costs while preserving tail-latency SLOs. This PR encodes heuristics from recent experiments, surfaces them through a small decision service, and provides tooling to simulate per-route unit economics. Changes: 1) autotune service: new microservice that ingests traffic profiles and outputs recommended batch_size, max_latency_target_ms, prefix_cache_ttl, and quant_profile. 2) runtime integration: runtime now accepts autotune hints (best-effort) for initial request routing and batching. 3) quant profiles: adds 8 curated profiles (fp16, int8-96, int8-8bit-legacy, q4_0, q4_1-compatible, q5_0, q8_0-sparse, mixed-quant-small) with metadata and compatibility matrix. 4) uecon tooling: CLI (tools/uecon) to simulate cost/perf for a given route, and an API endpoint (internal) to return per-100k-token cost estimates. 5) docs: single-page guide and ADR for autotune heuristics. Backwards compatibility: runtime ignores autotune hints if disabled; quant profiles are opt-in per model. Risks & mitigations: quant profiles are gated behind rollout flags and gradual canary; UEcon results are advisory only and flagged as experimental. Testing: unit tests for autotune decision logic, integration tests for runtime mapping, load tests showing median token-cost reduction of ~12% and P95 latency neutral under typical traffic shapes. See commits and CI below for details.

diff_snippets:
+ def recommend_batch_size(profile):
+     # heuristic: scale with qps and median_seq_len, but clamp for latency SLOs
+     suggested = max(1, int(profile.qps * 0.02))
+     return min(suggested, 256)

+ quant_profiles:
+   - name: q4_1-compatible
+     type: q4_1
+     supported_models: [gpt-small, gpt-medium]
+     expected_latency_multiplier: 1.05
review_comments: Elena Gomez (reviewer): Can we add an explicit safety check that prevents autotune from increasing batch size beyond what's been seen in canary traffic? We don't want sudden regressions in P99 latency.
Ravi Patel (author): Good point — added a 'canary_max_factor' clamp (default 1.2) and added unit tests. See commit l4m5n6.
Marco Chen (reviewer): The quant profiles list looks comprehensive. Add a compatibility matrix entry for the new q8_0-sparse profile and document when it's allowed (gpu only, cuda>=12.1).
Ravi Patel (author): Added matrix and a runtime check to only enable q8_0-sparse on supported hardware. Also added an e2e test that skips when hardware absent.

Priya Nair (SRE): CI load job initially failed due to an intermittent timeout in the load harness. I retriggered; the second run passed. Recommend monitoring the first-week rollout for increased error-rate signals.
Elena Gomez (reviewer): LGTM after the canary clamp + CI green. Approving.
Marco Chen (reviewer): Approving — also left one suggestion to make the uecon CLI output CSV by default for downstream analysis.

release_notes: Added autotune defaults engine to recommend batching/caching defaults and quantization profiles; added uecon tooling for per-route cost simulation. Quant profiles are opt-in and gated by rollout flags. Expected ~10-15% unit-cost savings for typical chat workloads. See docs/autotune-guide.md for migration and safety notes.
